samples.summary: Yorkie tree write ignores the superscript/subscript mutual exclusion that the cache write applies, so the CRDT keeps both flags while the local cache shows one
samples.evidence: `applyStyle` (line 1707) updates the cache with `applyInlineStyleHelper(block, from, to, style)`, and that helper (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:337-343) resolves `{superscript:true}` into `{superscript:true, subscript:undefined}` and, via `mergeInlineStyle` (block-helpers.ts:316-325), *deletes* `subscript` from the run. The tree path (`applyStyleInTree`, line 1716) is handed the RAW `style`: `serializeInlineStyle(style)` at line 1882 emits only `superscript:'true'` and `removedInlineStyleAttrs(style)` at line 1883 returns `[]` because `subscript` is not a key of the patch. Since `styleByPath` only merges, the pre-existing `subscript='true'` attribute survives on the Tree node. Ctrl+. on subscripted text (text-editor.ts:899) therefore leaves the CRDT with both `superscript` and `subscript` set; `parseInlineStyle` (line 168-173) reads both back on reload or on any remote-driven cache invalidation, so the run silently changes appearance/state relative to what the user saw. This is exactly the 'styleByPath cannot delete' class of bug the surrounding comment block (lines 1871-1881) claims is handled on this path.

samples.summary: Every style write, including the now-hot pure-clear toggle-off, re-asserts the node's full existing attribute map, which can clobber a concurrent remote attribute change
samples.evidence: `tree.styleByPath([...blockPath, i], { ...existingAttrs, ...styleAttrs })` re-sends every attribute already on the node even when `styleAttrs` is empty (the pure-clear case `{bold: undefined}` that, per the comment added at lines 1873-1875, is now every B/I/U/S toggle-off). The comment two lines above states styleByPath 'only merges', so passing `existingAttrs` is unnecessary; because it is sent with a fresh local timestamp, an LWW-per-attribute Tree resolves it over a concurrent peer's change to an unrelated attribute (e.g. peer sets `color` while this client toggles bold off), reverting the peer's edit. The delta puts this redundant full-attribute rewrite on the hottest editing path.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repo. block-helpers.ts:337-343 resolves superscript/subscript mutual exclusion for the cache write and mergeInlineStyle (316-325) deletes the undefined key, but yorkie-doc-store.ts:1716 (and 1760 in applyStyles) hands applyStyleInTree the RAW style patch. serializeInlineStyle (106-134) emits only the toggled key, and removedInlineStyleAttrs (144-163) requires `key in style && style[key] === undefined`, so a `{superscript:true}` patch yields no removals; styleByPath at line 1886 merges over existingAttrs, leaving the pre-existing subscript='true' attribute on the Tree node. The path is reachable with no intervening guard: text-editor.ts:899/905 -> toggleStyle (2858-2903, whose loop only sets the toggled key) -> applyStyleToSelection (2935) -> Doc.applyInlineStyle (model/document.ts:375-378), whose only patch rewrite styleOffAsClear (399-418) handles false->undefined and never the super/subscript pair. The divergence is observable: getDocument (544-546) serves the cache only while clean, and any reparse goes through parseInlineStyle (172-173), which reads both flags back; export code such as docx-style-map.ts:79-80 then emits two conflicting vertAlign elements. This is a broken invariant / CRDT-vs-cache state divergence, squarely in the correctness lane, and matches exactly the 'styleByPath cannot delete' hazard the comment at 1871-1881 claims to handle.

verdict.reason: The cited code exists verbatim: yorkie-doc-store.ts:1885-1886 reads the node's full attribute map and re-sends it via `tree.styleByPath([...blockPath, i], { ...existingAttrs, ...styleAttrs })`. Because `serializeInlineStyle` (lines 106-134) drops `undefined` values, the pure-clear case (`{bold: undefined}`) makes `styleAttrs` empty, so the write is a bare re-assertion of already-present attributes with a fresh local timestamp. The file itself documents that `styleByPath` "only merges attributes" (lines 137, 1872, 2509), so the `existingAttrs` spread is unnecessary for local correctness, and lines 1873-1875 confirm this now sits on every B/I/U/S toggle-off, i.e. the hottest editing path. Under per-attribute LWW resolution a redundant re-assert can beat a concurrent peer's change to an unrelated key (e.g. `color`), reverting it — an overwrite/incorrect-state-update squarely in the correctness lane. No guard, diffing, or caller-side narrowing exists (line 1886 is the only such call site), and the SDK (@yorkie-js/sdk 0.7.16, package.json:93) is not vendored, so I could not establish any value-equality short-circuit that would make the re-assert harmless. Nothing supports not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope.
